claims.text: A data-driven or machine-learning model incorporating phonon-dynamics and thermal-conductivity data can accurately predict the thermal-insulation properties of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed model will reduce mean absolute error by at least 15% relative to current predictions.
The approach applies to high-entropy alloys in as-cast or annealed states.
The approach applies to thermal-insulation operation between 300 K and 1000 K.
Phonon dynamics and thermal conductivity mediate the relationship between the model inputs and predicted insulation performance.
The machine-learning model captures complex relationships among phonon dynamics, thermal conductivity, and thermal-insulation properties.
Capturing those relationships produces more accurate predictions.
Current predictions are based on empirical rules and simplified models.
The model's applicability is limited to high-entropy alloys used for thermal insulation between 300 K and 1000 K.
The model may overfit or underfit and may have limited generalizability to other materials or applications.
Experimental thermal-conductivity and phonon-dynamics measurements can be used to validate the model against current predictions.
The hypothesis is falsified if the model's mean absolute error is not significantly lower than that of current predictions.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least a 15% MAE reduction, but the falsification rule tests only whether MAE is significantly lower. A statistically significant improvement smaller than 15% would fail the stated prediction without triggering the stated falsification rule.
The rule pairs 'not significantly lower' with p-value < 0.05, although p < 0.05 conventionally indicates statistical significance; this makes the criterion internally ambiguous.
